content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, the foreskin (and the state of being 'uncircumcised') symbolizes the unregenerate, sinful human nature ('the flesh') and, correspondingly, a heart that is closed, stubborn, and unresponsive to God. To be 'uncircumcised' is to stand outside God's covenant — impure, alienated, and spiritually insensible — while removal of the foreskin symbolizes the cutting away of sin and the cleansing/consecration of the person to God. This is developed into the metaphor of 'circumcision of the heart': physical foreskin removal typifies the inward removal of sinful resistance, accomplished ultimately (in Christian reading) by the Spirit through union with Christ rather than by the physical rite.", "primary_basis": ["Genesis 17:9-14 (circumcision as covenant sign; the uncircumcised male is 'cut off' from the covenant people)", "Deuteronomy 10:16 ('circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and be no longer stubborn')", "Deuteronomy 30:6 ('the LORD your God will circumcise your heart... so that you will love the LORD')", "Leviticus 26:41 ('uncircumcised heart' humbled)", "Jeremiah 4:4 ('circumcise yourselves to the LORD; remove the foreskin of your hearts')", "Jeremiah 6:10 ('their ears are uncircumcised, they cannot listen')", "Jeremiah 9:25-26 ('all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart')", "Ezekiel 44:7, 9 ('uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh' barred from the sanctuary)", "Acts 7:51 (Stephen: 'you stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears')", "Romans 2:25-29 ('circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not the letter')", "Philippians 3:3 ('we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God')", "Colossians 2:11-13 ('circumcision made without hands, by putting off the body of the flesh, the circumcision of Christ'; 'dead in... the uncircumcision of your flesh')", "Ephesians 2:11-13 (Gentiles 'called the uncircumcision'... 'alienated... strangers to the covenants' but brought near in Christ)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Ethnic/covenantal boundary marker: 'uncircumcised' functions simply as a label for outsiders to Israel — especially the Philistines and Gentiles generally — denoting foreignness and non-membership in the covenant people rather than an inner spiritual condition (e.g., Judges 14:3; 1 Samuel 17:26, 36; 2 Samuel 1:20; Ephesians 2:11; Galatians 2:7 where 'the uncircumcision' = Gentiles).", "basis": ["Judges 14:3", "1 Samuel 17:26, 36", "2 Samuel 1:20", "1 Samuel 31:4", "Ephesians 2:11", "Galatians 2:7-9", "Acts 11:3"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Ritual impurity/defilement reading: the foreskin represents cultic uncleanness and unfitness for God's presence; 'uncircumcised' pairs with 'unclean' as a purity category (Isaiah 52:1; Ezekiel 44:7-9), and its extension to 'uncircumcised' fruit trees (Leviticus 19:23) shows it marking something forbidden/unconsecrated rather than sinful per se.", "basis": ["Isaiah 52:1", "Ezekiel 44:7-9", "Leviticus 19:23-25", "Exodus 6:12, 30 ('uncircumcised lips' = unfitness to speak for God)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Fertility/fruitfulness reading (largely academic): circumcision, and the 'foreskin' of trees in Leviticus 19:23, symbolizes the removal of an obstruction to fruitfulness; the rite is tied to the promise of Abraham's abundant offspring, so the foreskin represents blocked or unconsecrated fertility.", "basis": ["Leviticus 19:23-25 (uncircumcised fruit)", "Genesis 17:2-6 (circumcision covenant joined to promise of multiplied offspring)", "Exodus 6:12 ('uncircumcised lips' as ineffective speech, by analogy)"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Shame/reproach reading: the foreskin embodies reproach or disgrace before God, removed at covenant renewal — e.g., Joshua 5 where circumcision at Gilgal 'rolls away the reproach of Egypt'; also foreskins as trophies of humiliation (1 Samuel 18:25-27).", "basis": ["Joshua 5:2-9", "Genesis 34:14 ('a disgrace to us')", "1 Samuel 18:25-27"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Christological/typological reading: the removal of the foreskin prefigures Christ's death — Colossians 2:11's 'circumcision of Christ' read as his crucifixion (the stripping off of his body), and patristic/medieval devotion to Christ's own circumcision as the first shedding of his blood for sin.", "basis": ["Colossians 2:11-12", "Luke 2:21", "Patristic and medieval exegesis (e.g., sermons on the Feast of the Circumcision)"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "There is a broadly settled and well-recognized symbolic tradition here, unusual in its explicitness: Scripture itself moralizes the term ('foreskin of your heart,' 'uncircumcised ears/lips'), so the primary meaning — the foreskin as the sinful, resistant 'flesh' whose removal signifies inner cleansing and covenant consecration — is stated within the biblical text and carried through virtually all major Christian streams (patristic, Reformation, Catholic, and modern evangelical exegesis). The alternatives listed are less rivals than complementary emphases: the ethnic-outsider usage and the impurity usage are both widely acknowledged as the literal/social senses on which the spiritual metaphor is built. Disagreement in scholarship concerns the rite's original function (fertility, apotropaism, tribal marking), not the settled theological symbolism of 'uncircumcision' as spiritual obduracy and alienation from God."}
